title: Cleared From The Board
description: Resolving a scheduling conflict by pulling one of the two overlapping cards off the board should make the conflict actually disappear — not just visually, but at the row level that the conflicts endpoint reads from.
successCondition: Create two assignments sharing the same driverId with overlapping windows (GET /api/fleet/conflicts now includes a "driver" entry naming both assignment ids). DELETE one of the two assignments. GET /api/fleet/conflicts no longer includes any conflict referencing either assignment id. Querying the assignments table via `npm run db:psql` confirms exactly one of the original two rows remains (matching whichever you didn't delete) — the conflict resolved because the underlying data actually changed, not because of any caching.
hints: GET /api/fleet/conflicts recomputes from the current assignments table on every call — there's no cached/stale conflicts list to worry about invalidating.
Note both assignment ids (not shipment ids) up front from the two PUT responses, since DELETE /api/fleet/assignments/:id takes the assignment's own id.
